title: GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst: What It Is and How to Use It
description: OpenAI's GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst is the precision tier of Images 2.6. Pricing, complexity, GIF and SVG output, plus runnable code.
author: freellm.site
content:
**GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst is OpenAI's high-detail image generation and editing model, released on November 4, 2026 as part of Images 2.6, with the API model ID `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`.** It's one of a pair: Sunburst handles dense compositions, text-heavy layouts and edits that must stay consistent, while GPT Image 2.6 Flare is built for speed. OpenAI says the 2.6 generation produces images about 50% faster than the previous one.

![GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst: What It Is and How to Use It](/images/blog/gpt-image-2-6-sunburst-guide/image-0.jpg)

If you came here from an OpenRouter model page: Sunburst isn't a stealth model or a leak. It's a documented OpenAI production model, available through OpenAI's Image API and resold through aggregators like [OpenRouter](/providers/openrouter/). Below is what's new, what it costs, and a request you can copy and run.

## What GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst is

Per [OpenAI's model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst.md), Sunburst takes **text and image inputs** and produces **image outputs**. So it's both a generator (prompt in, picture out) and an editor (image plus prompt in, revised picture out).

The [Images 2.6 announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-images-2-6/) splits the two models by job:

- **Flare** is for fast iteration. With `quality` set to low, OpenAI says it can generate an image in as little as six seconds. It also lays out posters and product imagery better.
- **Sunburst** is for detail and precision. OpenAI says it produces higher-quality images and keeps them *more consistent across edits* when quality is set to medium or high.

Edit consistency is what sets Sunburst apart. For one-shot generation, Flare is probably fine. If you're doing round after round of "keep the character, change the background," Sunburst is the model that keeps the character intact.

For scale, OpenAI says people now create **4 billion images per week** across ChatGPT, Codex and the API.

## What's new in 2.6

The 2.6 pair adds four capabilities, and all of them apply to both Sunburst and Flare through the Image API.

### 1. The `complexity` parameter

This is the biggest change for developers. `complexity` controls **how much the model plans before it renders**, separately from `quality`, which controls how detailed the render is.

From the [image generation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation):

- Supported levels are `low`, `medium`, and `high`.
- If you omit it, **both models default to `high`**.
- Lower complexity suits focused edits, such as changing a background or swapping a sign.
- Higher complexity helps with dense text, complex layouts, and relationships between objects.
- Higher complexity **can increase latency and introduce unwanted changes**, so OpenAI tells you to compare results for your task.
- Adjusting complexity carries **no separate fee**.

For most editing work, OpenAI recommends low complexity for faster edits, combined with whatever image quality your workflow needs.

A simple way to decide: if the layout is right but small text is unreadable, raise `quality` and leave `complexity` alone. If the composition itself is wrong, raise complexity.

### 2. Markup-guided edits in the API

Image markup, where you draw on an image to show exactly what should change, was already in ChatGPT. With 2.6 it reaches the API, so you can mark specific regions instead of describing them in words.

### 3. SVG output

Sunburst can export vector images. Per [Replicate's model documentation](https://replicate.com/openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst), this happens in two stages: the model renders a raster image, then a text model traces it into SVG paths. SVG works for **generation only**, one image per request, and you're billed for the image tokens *plus* the tracing model's tokens. Simple logos cost less than detailed scenes.

### 4. Animated GIF output

Set the output format to `gif` and you get a looping animation. Replicate documents the settings: `frame_count` from 2 to 16 (default 9) and `frame_duration_ms` from 20 to 2000 (default 200), so the nine default frames loop in 1.8 seconds. All frames share one image budget, which makes GIF frames smaller: 1:1 renders at 512×512 and 16:9 at 896×512. Describe the motion *and* the loop in your prompt ("the lantern sways, then returns to its starting position, smooth loop"), not only the subject.

## Pricing

OpenAI prices Sunburst by tokens, and, which surprises people, **exactly the same as Flare**:

| Metric | Price | Unit |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Text input | $5 | 1M tokens |
| Text cached input | $1.25 | 1M tokens |
| Image input | $8 | 1M tokens |
| Image cached input | $2 | 1M tokens |
| Image output | $30 | 1M tokens |

Price doesn't decide between Sunburst and Flare; you're trading latency against fidelity. You pay for the tokens you use, and higher `quality` settings use more output tokens.

OpenRouter lists the same $8 in / $30 per 1M for `openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, served by one provider. Its public playground example gives a sense of real cost: a 16:9 image at 1536×864 took 44.7 seconds and cost **$0.03292**. That's one data point, since complexity, quality and prompt length all change it.

## Sunburst vs Flare vs 2.5 Sunburst

| | GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst | GPT Image 2.6 Flare | GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Model ID | `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` |
| Positioned for | Detail, precision, edit accuracy | Fast iteration, interactive work | Precision tier of the 2.5 series |
| Speed claim | ~50% faster than prior generation | ~50% faster; as little as 6s at low quality | Baseline |
| `complexity` setting | Yes | Yes | No |
| GIF / SVG output | Yes | Yes | No |
| Markup-guided edits via API | Yes | Yes | No |
| Price (image in / out) | $8 / $30 per 1M | $8 / $30 per 1M | Check the pricing page |

Pick Flare when response time matters more than fine detail. Pick Sunburst when an image has strict requirements for detail, layout or edit accuracy.

## How to call it

Sunburst is served on the Image API endpoints. The model page lists `v1/images/generations` and `v1/images/edits` as **supported** and marks Chat Completions, Responses, Batch, Embeddings and the rest as not supported for this model ID, so you can't drop it into a chat-completions wrapper. (OpenAI's guide does describe an `image_generation` tool inside the Responses API, but the published examples still reference 2.5 model IDs, so check current tool support in the docs before you build on it.)

A minimal generation request:

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2.6-sunburst",
    "prompt": "A hand-bent warm-white neon sign in flowing cursive reading FREELLM above a dark storefront at blue hour, wet pavement reflections, no people.",
    "quality": "high",
    "complexity": "high",
    "size": "1536x1024"
  }'
```

And in Python, saving the result to disk:

```python
import base64
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])

result = client.images.generate(
    model="gpt-image-2.6-sunburst",
    prompt=(
        "Editorial product shot of a matte black mechanical keyboard on "
        "concrete, single hard key light from the left, deep shadows, "
        "shallow depth of field."
    ),
    quality="high",
    # Lower this to 'low' for focused edits; 'high' is the default.
    extra_body={"complexity": "high"},
    size="1536x1024",
)

with open("keyboard.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(base64.b64decode(result.data[0].b64_json))

print("wrote keyboard.png")
```

Two practical notes. `complexity` is a newer field, so if your installed SDK version predates it, pass it through `extra_body` as above instead of as a named argument. And OpenAI notes you may need to complete **API Organization Verification** in your developer console before using GPT Image models at all. That's the most common reason a correct-looking request returns a 403.

On sizes: OpenRouter documents quality tiers from low through max, transparent background support, and custom sizes in **multiples of 16 pixels** at aspect ratios from **1:3 to 3:1**. Replicate lists the quality enum as `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or `auto` (the default). Start at `low` for drafts and save `xhigh`/`max` for final assets, since you pay per output token either way.

Nobody outside your account can tell you your rate limits. They vary by usage tier and account, so check your organization's limits page.

## Where this sits in 2026

Image models have become infrastructure rather than a novelty, the same path text models took, as we covered in [the state of AI in 2026](/blog/state-of-ai-2026-snapshot/). The notable change in 2.6 is the focus on *editing*, not prettier pictures. A `complexity` dial, markup-guided regional edits and consistency across edits are all features for people on their tenth revision.

If you're putting Sunburst into a pipeline, consider going through an aggregator. A gateway gives you one key across many models, which helps when you want to A/B Sunburst against Gemini-family image models without rewriting your client; our guide to [OpenAI-compatible APIs](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) shows the pattern. If you're prototyping on a budget before paying for image generation, our roundup of the [best free LLM APIs in 2026](/blog/best-free-llm-apis-2026/) covers the text side of that stack, and [Muse Spark Open](/blog/muse-spark-open-meta-guide/) shows how fast the open-weight end of the market is moving.

For safety behaviour and evaluation methodology, OpenAI published a [system card for ChatGPT Images 2.6](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/chatgpt-images-2-6) that compares 2.6 Sunburst and Flare against their 2.5 baselines.

## FAQ

### Is GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst the same as the OpenRouter "Sunburst" model?

Yes. OpenRouter lists it as `openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, released November 4, 2026, served by one provider. It's OpenAI's model resold through OpenRouter's unified API, not a separate or stealth model. The listing also shows a 400K context figure and the same $8 in / $30 per 1M pricing.

### Should I use Sunburst or Flare?

Use Flare when speed matters more than fine detail; OpenAI says it can return an image in as little as six seconds at low quality. Use Sunburst when the image has strict detail, layout or edit-accuracy requirements, and when you need consistency across several rounds of edits at medium or high quality. Both cost the same per token.

### Does raising `complexity` cost more?

No. OpenAI says explicitly that adjusting complexity has no separate fee. It can increase latency and introduce changes you didn't ask for, though, so OpenAI recommends low complexity for most focused edits and medium or high for scenes with many elements or constraints.

### Can I use GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst through Chat Completions?

Not directly. The model page marks `v1/images/generations` and `v1/images/edits` as supported and Chat Completions, Responses, Batch and the others as not supported for this model ID. Use the Image API, and check the official docs for the current state of the Responses API image-generation tool.

### Is there a free tier for GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst?

OpenAI's published pricing is token-based, and the model documentation mentions no free allowance, so budget for paid usage and check the official pricing page for current terms. Images 2.6 is available in ChatGPT and Codex on every subscription tier, which is the cheapest way to try the model before writing any API code.
